definitions.explanation: An area where there is significant risk to safety or life — due to natural hazards, conflict, crime, or industrial conditions. Used literally on warning signs and figuratively in casual speech.

examples.japanese: ここは{危険地帯|きけんちたい}だ。
{台風|たいふう}の{影響|えいきょう}でこの{地域|ちいき}は{危険地帯|きけんちたい}となっている。
examples.english: Because of the typhoon, this area has become a danger zone.

examples.japanese: {戦争|せんそう}{中|ちゅう}の{国|くに}には{危険地帯|きけんちたい}が{広|ひろ}がっており、{民間人|みんかんじん}の{出入|でい}りが{禁止|きんし}されている。
examples.english: Danger zones have spread across the country at war, and civilian entry is prohibited.

notes:
Compound of {危険|きけん} (danger) + {地帯|ちたい} (zone, area). Used in news reporting, official warnings, and casually to describe any unsafe place.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {危険地帯|きけんちたい}に{入|はい}る: to enter a danger zone
- {危険地帯|きけんちたい}を{避|さ}ける: to avoid a danger zone
- {危険地帯|きけんちたい}に{指定|してい}される: to be designated a danger zone
- {紛争|ふんそう}{危険地帯|きけんちたい}: conflict zone

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {警戒区域|けいかいくいき}: caution/restricted area — official designation, often after disasters
- {立入禁止区域|たちいりきんしくいき}: no-entry zone — focuses on the prohibition, not the danger itself
